description: Figshare proper (10.6084) cannot be a prefix discard: D1 dropped it from `deposit-registrant` because individuals self-deposit real manuscripts there, and a read of the 79 rows on the prefix in release 8c363ade confirms both halves — most are attachments of a published paper ("Supplementary material from …", "Additional file 2: of …", "R codes (main analyses) …", "Methods Video for …", raw-data bundles, and files whose title IS a filename), but a genuine tail of registered reports and self-deposited replication manuscripts remains. So the discard is scoped by what the record says it is: the prefix AND a title that announces an attachment rather than a study. The patterns are deliberately front-anchored or filename-shaped so that a paper ABOUT supplementary analyses is not caught; a figshare record whose title reads as a study title falls through to the admission band and buys its screening like any other row — 14 of the 79 do, which is the point, not a leak. The parent paper of a discarded attachment is expected in the corpus under its own DOI (same residual-loss posture as `deposit-registrant`, tracked by #157). Sits with the definitional discards, below `deposit-registrant` (958): that rule's claim is about who mints the DOI, this one's is about what the record's own title declares.

measured.rationale: Maintainer decision 2026-08-05, wording confirmed against the full population on the prefix in release 8c363ade: 79 rows, 55 matched by these patterns (all unambiguous attachments on read), 14 kept — every kept title reads as a study or is at worst an ambiguous attachment the screen rejects for two cents. The claim is structural (the title's own words), so `trusted`; the residual risk is an attachment titled like a paper, which the screen — not this rule — then judges.
